name: Manmohan Singh
role: Prime Minister of India (2004-2014); Finance Minister (1991-1996)
summary: Singh, an economist, led India's 1991 shift away from licensing and import controls toward markets and foreign investment, while keeping a state role in planning and social programmes. As prime minister he pursued the civil nuclear agreement with the United States, an employment guarantee and inclusive-growth programmes, and an independent foreign policy, and defended Parliament's authority over law.

notes: Searched, by theme (foreign alliances, intervention, nationalism and the pluralism line were searched last: non-alignment summit speeches, Iraq, Syria, Afghanistan, Pakistan, Kashmir and the armed forces special powers act turned up only press summaries or remarks that settle none of the statements): economy (1991 budget, 2006 National Development Council address, rural employment guarantee), government (Lokpal statements of August 2011, confidence-motion reply of 2008), world (four UN General Assembly speeches, nuclear agreement, Iraq, Palestine, UN reform), ecology (climate change, energy), liberty (surveillance, death penalty, none found), society and culture (religion, family, gender; only general remarks on minorities and women found). His 2006 line that minorities, particularly Muslims, must have first claim on resources was read in the full text: it sits in a list of priority groups and does not state a position on any statement, so it is not used. His 2005 Oxford speech survives here only as a blog excerpt, so it is not cited. The press reports of his 2014 farewell press conference (on the 2002 Gujarat riots and Narendra Modi) state no position on any statement. Many statements on society, culture, liberty and technology are null because the sources opened say nothing on them. Record over words: the economy answers rest on the 1991 measures, not his speeches; the Lokpal answers are words because the sources opened report only what he said.
